correctness.rationale: The standard PALF handle complex has \(C_2\cong\mathbb Z^6\to C_1\cong\mathbb Z^5\) with boundary matrix \(V\) whose columns are the six published vanishing-cycle classes. Exact determinantal divisors \(1,1,1,1,4\) give Smith form \(\operatorname{diag}(1,1,1,1,4)\), hence \(H_1\cong\mathbb Z/4\) and \(H_2\cong\mathbb Z\). The cochain matrix is \(V^{\mathsf T}\), so \(H^2\cong\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/4\). Mori proves \([\mathbf 1_6]\ne0\) and \(2[\mathbf 1_6]=0\); therefore that \(c_1\) is the unique order-two element of the cyclic torsion summand.

Mori proves that the associated \(c_1\) is nonzero of order two and records \(\ker V\), but does not determine \(\operatorname{coker}V\), the Smith form, or the complete \(H^2\) group. value.rationale: Mori highlights this exact generalized-lantern example because a relation-only test misses torsion. The Smith form resolves the natural structural question left open by that warning: the hidden torsion is exactly cyclic order four, and the Chern obstruction is its unique order-two element. This distinguishes the example from one having only \(\mathbb Z/2\) torsion and makes the integrality failure completely explicit.
